reason: Schedule and feasibility lens. The engineering is cheap and runtime is safe. The plan still cannot produce a readable scored probe by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC with >= 70% probability. (1) The probe is gated on a lab result the idea itself puts at P~0.25 (lab gain >= +0.001 on both embryos). Logistics are ~0.85, so P(a gate-passing probe is scored) is ~0.2. (2) As written, the lab runs on friend A's 5070 Ti PC. He has been silent since 24 Sep, his queue after #34 is the x138 cache and H2, and the pass is ~3-7 h, not 3 h: 199 videos x 1-2 min. The idea's own path is 52 h to a score (Sun 27 16:00Z), with P(friend A in time) ~0.5, so ~0.1 overall. (3) The lab bed is not the shipped base. exp39 tails have no V1284 head, and no x138 train tails exist (sibling verdicts: 13-16 GPU-h to build them). The gate therefore measures the correction on top of exp39 positions (mean error 1.686 um), not on top of the head (1.525 um). That overstates the gain the ship would see. (4) The output path is not what the idea assumes. x138's writer rounds z/y/x to int (exp56 cell 5, write_test_submission). tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.13-14 allows only divinsert/leafprune on --base x138, so floatout must be ported (+1-2 h). Its 'safe' mode encodes only non-negative fractions (w = r + clip(v-r, 0, 0.499)), so about half of every sub-voxel shift is discarded. A shift of <= 0.6 um (w 0.4 x clip 1.5) is also mostly erased in z (1.625 um voxels). (5) Even when scored, the probe cannot be read: expected public gain 0..+0.001 against LB noise ~0.003 (BRIEF s.1), so one slot answers nothing. Checked OK: head numbers (out_full_P/report.txt: leak5 folds none 1.63-1.73 / public 1.45-1.60 / new 1.21-1.28 um, 125,700 pairs), x138's refine_synthetic_midpoint touching only synthetic nodes, and runtime. My container benchmark gives 0.76 ms/node for crop-local Gaussian+Otsu+watershed. The hidden test (~100-130 videos, CONTEXT.md l.14) at 5k-30k nodes/video comes to ~8-45 min single-thread, far from the 12 h limit. The one risk is placement: the 27,000 s REPAIR_DEADLINE_S check sits inside the per-movie writer loop, and added per-movie time pushes later movies into the degraded no-relink mode.
fix_if_any: Remove friend A and test on the shipped coordinates. (a) Localisation gate on the head, not on exp39. On the user's laptop, export the public-head positions for all kept peaks from experiments/coordhead_retrain/captures (313,205 kept peaks, 125,700 GT pairs), with the GT pairs, as a small parquet. Upload it and experiments/l2_daughternet/coords_exp39.parquet (11 MB, already in the repo) as private Kaggle datasets. (b) Run one free Kaggle CPU kernel with the competition data mounted. It reads the train zarr frames with the same blosc2 reader as read_test_frame and computes the crop watershed centroid (fixed w 0.4, clip 1.5 um, neighbours as markers, only nodes within 9 um of a GT node). It writes refined coords keyed by (stem, node_id) and by capture peak. Cost: ~1 h, no GPU quota. (c) Gate, pre-registered, per embryo. On head positions: mean distance down >= 5% and share<=4um not lower. On exp39 tails: laptop replay.py with a new out.coord_override knob, official score >= +0.001 overall and >= 0 on each embryo. (d) Kernel patch 'wscentroid' for --base x138. It runs after linefit and only when elapsed < REPAIR_DEADLINE_S - 1800 and not _deadline_degraded, and at ENABLE=0 it is byte-identical. It is ported together with floatout for x138, using mode 'float' if the exp52 parity run proved the server parses floats; otherwise safe mode, accepting the loss. (e) Ship only as a rider on an already-planned x138 carrier (with a twin control), never as a solo slot, because +0.001 is below LB noise. This makes the logistics ~0.85, but P(gate pass) stays ~0.25-0.3, so P(a scored, gate-passing rider) is ~0.2-0.25.
